prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: how many units did store BE-14 sell in 2024, as stored and with resent copies removed? These tables may hold errors. Two lines are copies of one order line when order_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price_eur, promo_id and line_discount_eur all match, with a missing promo_id matching a missing one; keep one line of each such set. 2024 means order_ts, as stored, from 1 January 2024 up to but not including 1 January 2025. Return two columns, in this order: units_stored and units_unique. The result is a single row. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, check which columns the DISTINCT step compares.
Each resent copy has an order_line_id of its own, so a DISTINCT that keeps order_line_id keeps every copy too.
starter_sql:
WITH be14_lines AS (  -- one row per BE-14 order line of 2024, as stored
  SELECT ol.order_line_id, ol.order_id, ol.product_id, ol.quantity, ol.unit_price_eur, ol.promo_id, ol.line_discount_eur
  FROM order_lines ol
  JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = ol.order_id
  JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
  WHERE s.store_code = 'BE-14'
    AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
),
unique_lines AS (  -- one row per order line, copies removed
  SELECT DISTINCT order_line_id, order_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price_eur, promo_id, line_discount_eur
  FROM be14_lines
)
SELECT (SELECT SUM(quantity) FROM be14_lines) AS units_stored,
       (SELECT SUM(quantity) FROM unique_lines) AS units_unique
why_this_works: Leaving order_line_id out of the DISTINCT lets a copy and its original collapse into one line, so its units count once.
